name: Polyvinylidene fluoride
description: Polyvinylidene fluoride (CAS 24937-79-9 ), commonly known as PVDF, is a high-performance fluoropolymer resin used across demanding industrial applications where chemical resistance and thermal stability are non-negotiable sourcing criteria. It functions as a structural and functional material in environments where conventional polymers fail. This material enables long service life in aggressive chemical, electrical, and outdoor exposure conditions for global manufacturers. In the electronics and battery industries, PVDF serves as the primary binder material for lithium-ion battery electrode coatings. This application directly influences cell performance and cycle life in modern energy storage systems. Piping systems, pumps, valves, and tank linings for chemical processing rely on PVDF where resistance to acids, solvents, and halogens is required. It provides a robust solution for high-purity fluid handling and transport. Architectural coatings and building facade systems use PVDF-based formulations to deliver weathering resistance and color retention over decades. These coatings protect structures from UV degradation and harsh environmental pollutants. In filtration membranes for water treatment and pharmaceutical processing, PVDF is the base polymer of choice. It is favored due to its ability to be cast into microporous structures with controlled pore geometry. PVDF is supplied as powder, pellets, and solution-grade dispersions depending on the processing method. Injection molding, extrusion, or coating applications each require distinct forms to ensure optimal manufacturing results. Standard grades include homopolymer and copolymer variants, with battery-grade and membrane-grade specifications available.
